testingFeedback: About 12 real bugs and about a dozen harness problems. Three were game-breaking: the results screen did not open after the first match of a session; the dev panel freeze stayed on after closing; a penalty kicked to touch froze the ball.
Three game-breaking issues (see the first answer).
The scripted whole-cup playthrough with an autopilot in the human's seat: it caught the results and cup bugs.
The tackle success test over 400 tries: it checked a formula against itself and passed on the first run.
engineFeedback: The scene, input, TileMap, Humanoid and Dialog APIs did what the API card said.
Stuck: saves use localStorage, which does not exist in Node, so headless tests needed an in-memory stand-in. Also the Dialog's voice blip is per page, so per-letter babble needed game code.
Built by hand: the rugby simulation, set pieces, the CPU brain, the HUD, commentary and babble, and the dev panel.
Hardest: TileMap wall heights and camera framing, and drawing rigs in the right order over the stands.
I would change one thing: a headless Dialog and menu test API, so UI flows could be checked without a browser.
promptFeedback: The plan is very thorough and says exactly what each system should do, with numbers.
The plan and TASK.md disagree on the title and file names; TASK.md has to win, and the plan's scope is far beyond one session.
Writing a full sports sim with set pieces, AI and tests in one pass was the hardest part.
Ship a smaller first milestone with a clear cut list, and say which features are required for the demo.

aiHub.name: SMASHBY
aiHub.tagline: Big hits, bigger hair, seven a side
aiHub.description: Over-the-top arcade rugby sevens: turbo runs, big hits, a referee who only sees some of it, and a pub team's run at the Mega Cup.
aiHub.controls: Left stick or WASD run, R2 or Shift turbo, Cross or Space tackle or step, Circle or C kick, L1/R1 or Q/E pass, Triangle or R super
